name: Phase Exit Review Checklist
one_liner: The gate self-assessment — four sheets of questions the PM answers before asking the PSC to let the project through.
purpose: Phase-Exit Review Checklists are spreadsheet-based documents used by the Project Manager (PM) to ensure that all the necessary items are in place before the project proceeds to the next phase or is closed. They check the key information of each phase and gather Lessons Learned. PM² provides one checklist per phase, used alongside a review of that phase's specific goals to support the RfP, RfE and RfC gate decisions.
created_in: Monitor & Control — run at the end of each phase, from Initiating onwards
approved_by: Not formally approved: the PM completes it and the Project Steering Committee (PSC) approves the phase transition it supports (the AGB if deviations from the Business Case or Charter are material)
inputs: The phase's own artefacts and deliverables
feeds: Phase gate decision: RfP, RfE, RfC
Lessons Learned in the Project-End Report
gate: RfP · RfE · RfC (one sheet per gate, plus a Closing sheet)

lifecycle.what: Initiating sheet completed; supports the RfP gate decision
Planning sheet completed; supports the RfE gate decision

traps: It is not approved by anyone — the PM completes it; the PSC approves the phase transition.
There is no RASCI row for it in the guide; it is an output of Manage Quality (SP=A, PM=R).
One workbook, four sheets, three gates — the Closing sheet sits after RfC, not at a gate.
A high score is not a gate pass: the PSC still decides, guided by the phase's own goals.
Do not confuse it with the Quality Review Checklist (deliverable quality) or the Business Implementation Checklist.
